doc.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 5, 2021 [interview 2 of 2]

title: No career goals; jobs came by phone call; doctor's call interrupts
summary: Gibbs says he never had goals and was called by Goodman, Herman, Allen and Philbin; a phone call from his doctor's office interrupts.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well this is sort of a two part question. I wonder if you had definite goals for a life in music and did your mother support them? Did she think you were going into the right career?

Well it started like I never had goals. I never had goals. And I’ve been blessed things fell in my lap. I never would have auditioned with Benny Goodman, he called me. I never auditioned with Woody Herman, he called me. I never auditioned with Steve Allen, Regis Philbin, they called me. So I’ve been blessed in that way, and I never had goals. I wanted to play good. That was my goal if anything, I just wanted to play to where I enjoyed it. I never, you know it’s wild to say I never play for an audience. I play for me. I hope they like what I’m doing. By the way there’s a call for you, Monk.
Okay yes that’s — I’m going to catch a plan out there and get that.
You know it’s my doctor but I’m not going to answer it. I want to see what he has to say.
Okay we can cut this out. Message from doctor’s office reminder of appointment.
